To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the equilibrium positions of the Calogero-Moses system for each root system are given by a family of polynomials which are orthogonal with respect to the weight function w = e−2V, where V is the potential energy, and which satisfy the differential equation d2y/dt2 + V′′(t)y = λy, which is equivalent to the eigenvalue problem for the Lax pair matrix.

the equilibrium positions of the classical Calogero-Sutherland system are associated with the zeros of classical orthogonal polynomials and that the equilibrium positions in the exceptional and non-crystal-lographic Calogero-Suthe-rland systems are associated with zeros of new polynomials which we call the exceptional and non-crys-tallographic polynomials.
the equilibrium positions of Calorgero and Sutherland systems correspond to the zeros, and their minimum energies to the roots, of the classical orthogonal polynomials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the zeros of the polynomials associated with the exceptional root systems and the non-crystallographical root systems.
the following three problems.

the zeros of polynomials, their properties, their relationship with the Calogero-Maser systems, and the relationship between the zeros of the polynomials and the equilibrium positions of the Calogero-Sutherland systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the equilibrium positions of classical Calogeros and Sutherlands are the zeros of the classical orthogonal polynomials and those for exceptional and non-crystallo- graphic root systems are the zeros of polynomials which are related to the classical polynomials in the same way that the exceptional and non-crystalline root systems are related to the crystallographic ones.

all the equilibrium positions of classical and exceptional Calogero-Sutherland systems can be associated with the zeros of the polynomials of Jacobi-Anger, Hermite, Laguerrre, Jacobi, Chebyshev, Legendre, Gegenbauer, Bessel, Krawtchouk and Meixner polynomials.
the equilibrium positions of Calogeromoser systems are associated with polynomials which are orthogonal in a generalized sense, i.e. with polynomials that satisfy a three-term recurrence relation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all the equilibrium positions in Calogero and/or Sutherland systems for all root systems (classical, exceptional and non-crystal-lographic) are associated with some polynomials.
all the equilibrium points of Calogero-Mosersystems are associated with polynomials.
the equilibrium positions for Calogero and/or Sutherland systems with the classical and exceptional root systems are associated with the zeros of classical and exceptional orthogonal polynomials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classical and exceptional polynomials can be derived from a single generating function.
the equilibrium points of Calogero-Mosersystems are related to polynomials associated with the root systems.

these polynomials are associated with the eigenvalues of the Lax pair matrices and the frequencies of small oscillation at the equilibrium positions of the corresponding Calogero and Calogero-Morse systems.
